proofs.text: Run `--gate tested` and verify no workflow; run `--gate recorded` and verify `.github/workflows/purlin.yml` exists; run `--gate approved` and verify the workflow's bytes are unchanged and the summary reports it as kept; run `--gate tested` again and verify the config reads `tested` with `min_strength` 50 while the workflow is still there; set `approvers` to `["jane@acme.com"]`, run `--gate recorded` and verify the list survives

rule_text: Raising the gate adds what the higher level needs and keeps every file an earlier run wrote; lowering it writes the setting and deletes nothing, the approver list included

tests.body:
def test_raising_to_recorded_adds_the_workflow(self, project):
        project.run('--gate', 'tested')
        assert not project.has('.github/workflows/purlin.yml')
        project.run('--gate', 'recorded')
        assert project.has('.github/workflows/purlin.yml')
        assert project.config()['gate'] == 'recorded'
tests.name: test_lowering_from_approved_keeps_the_approver_list
reasons: expected value computed by same function as SUT
